The moat

The Trade Graph compounds.

Every transaction adds delivery, dispute, inspection and payment data to a proprietary network. Over time, TradeOS knows who actually ships — a dataset no incumbent can back-fill. Hover the nodes.

Proactive trade intelligence

We don't wait for demand. We see it coming.

Every search and deal feeds a demand model. When a category heats up, TradeOS alerts capable factories to add capacity before the rush — and tells buyers who'll be ready. Passive dashboards report the past; the Signal Engine acts on the future.

Demand, turned into action.

A factory that tools up a month early wins the order. A buyer who knows who's ready skips the scramble. TradeOS sits in the middle and routes the signal both ways — a second moat on top of the Trade Graph.

  • Forecasts, not dashboards — corridor-level demand spikes detected weeks ahead.
  • Push, not pull — capable factories are notified to spin up the right capacity.
  • A paid signal — factories pay for the lead; buyers get shorter lead times.

The broker guild · ecosystem foundation

Don't cut out the broker. Verify them.

80% of high-value machinery still trades through brokers, agents and trading houses — relationships built over years. Every other platform tries to delete them, which is exactly why those deals stay offline. TradeOS does the opposite: the broker network is the foundation of the platform, brought on as verified, scored participants. Not a feature — the operating model.

  • Real-time Broker Trust Score — updates after every deal; brokers see exactly what's hurting it and improve.
  • Compete and cooperate — score drives premium deal flow, yet brokers still need each other to close cross-border.
  • Disclosed commissions — no hidden margins; buyers see the fee before they commit.
  • Reputational skin in the game — a broker's score follows every deal they touch.
